source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
Corn can be harvested for eating or for sale as follows: for sweet corn, harvest after the plant is 65 days old or more, or about 18-22 days after silk emergence (when the silk has dried). For grain corn, harvest when kernels are fully developed with a tight, firm husk and the silk has dried.

Harvesting should be done in the early morning or in the evening, and harvested ears should be kept in a shaded location.

Ears should be moved from the field to the packing area immediately, where they should be sorted by type/grade and cooled quickly, because sweet corn loses 50% or more of its sugar content within 24 hours if not cooled promptly. Sweet corn must also be kept cool during transport. To achieve the highest quality and value, sweet corn must be kept continuously cool and under proper conditions from harvest until it reaches the consumer. Sweet corn is typically packed in plastic sacks that hold about 4-6 dozen ears, depending on sack size and ear size. Ears are transported to wholesale markets, then repacked into new poly bags before being sold on to wholesalers and retailers.
